composition.mass: Seen from beetle height, the drawing's lower third becomes the whole world: two humus masses, the big one heaped with root knees, joined by the fallen log as a plank bridge, lit from within by pale mycelium lamps, with red toadstools and lichen duff along the path.
composition.read: Across the low duff bank past lichen hummocks and toadstools, over the fallen-log bridge, and up through root knees to the bird.

lighting.notes: fungus glow under a closed canopy: The drawing's floor is its darkest zone (#333333 in the root crevices); under a closed canopy the light comes from the ground itself, so a dim green background and pale mycelium lamps carry it.

concept.name: aspect-roots
concept.fragment: Round 5 reading authored by the build agent from pipeline/seed/analysis/forest.json and the drawing itself, without the analyzer (Gemini returns 402). One aspect of the charcoal drawing, "roots", becomes the place; the shaper, palette, lighting, props and the figure's pose are argued from that aspect alone. It must not repeat the round-4 forest readings (ash basin with soot trunks, taproot knoll with charred boles, birch spiral) or their shapers (basin, mound, spiral).
